handbook: University Assessment Handbook (synthetic example). Assignments should be uploaded through the learning portal before the stated deadline. Late submission is normally penalized according to the course rules. Students who experience illness may request an extension, but they must provide medical evidence before the original deadline. The coordinator reviews the request and confirms the decision. A request does not automatically approve an extension. Students should keep a copy of the submitted file and the confirmation message. The final assignment file should be a PDF unless the teacher gives another format. If the portal is unavailable, students should take a screenshot of the error and contact the course help desk before the deadline. The help desk records the time of the report, but it does not approve academic extensions. Students should include their course code and assignment title in support messages. This synthetic handbook is for programming practice only and is not a real university policy. The general late rule and illness exception must be read together. A student should not rely on one sentence without checking the related exception and current course instructions.
it_help: IT Help Guide (synthetic example). A forgotten account password can be reset by opening the login page and selecting the recovery link. The user should follow the instructions sent to their registered email address. Never share a password or recovery code with another person. If the recovery email does not arrive, check the spam folder and confirm that the account email is correct. After several failed attempts, contact the help desk and provide the account username, but do not send the password. The help desk may ask the user to verify account ownership. API tokens are different from account passwords. In the example software version 2, an expired API token is renewed by sending POST /v2/token/refresh and including the refresh_token field. Do not print token values in logs. Version 1 uses POST /v1/auth/renew instead. Always check the version of the documentation before following instructions. This is fictional instructional text and not a live service or real credential procedure.
returns: Customer Returns Guide (synthetic example). If a parcel arrives damaged, contact customer support within 48 hours of delivery. Attach clear photographs of the damaged item and its packaging. Keep the parcel and packaging until support provides instructions. The support team may request the order number, but customers should not post private order information publicly. A change-of-mind return is different from a damage report. For a change of mind, unused items may be returned within 14 days under this fictional example. Damage reports in a different region have a 72-hour reporting window, so region information must be checked before giving advice. These rules are synthetic and are not actual company policies. A response should include the reporting deadline and the required photographs together. If a customer misses the deadline, the text does not promise an exception. The support team reviews each report and provides the next steps. Do not confuse damaged goods with a normal return or use another region's deadline.
workplace: Remote Work Policy (synthetic example). Employees may request remote work when their manager approves the arrangement. Approval depends on job duties, team needs and the written agreement. Contractors are not covered by the employee rule. A contractor may work remotely only when the signed contract explicitly permits remote work. A verbal statement does not replace the contract condition in this example. The employee policy must not be used to answer a contractor question. Staff should check the policy version and their employment category before relying on a passage. This document is a fictional classroom dataset and does not describe an actual employer. If the contract is unclear, the person should ask the contract owner or HR contact for clarification. Remote work approval is not automatic for either category. The contractor exception is important because a general remote-work passage could appear relevant while omitting the contractual condition. Keep the eligibility rule and its exception in the same evidence passage when possible.
printer: Printer Troubleshooting Guide (synthetic example). If a printer has power but produces blank pages, first check the ink or toner level. Next, run the printer cleaning utility from the device menu. Then print a test page and inspect the result. Follow the device manual and do not open electrical components while the printer is connected to power. A blank scanner image is a different problem: check document placement and select the correct scanning source. Do not apply scanner instructions to a printer. If the printer still produces blank pages, check that the cartridge is installed correctly and contact technical support. Keep the order of the steps because the first checks are simple and safe. This guide is fictional and may not match every device model. The model number should be checked before performing maintenance. A warning or safety instruction should remain close to the troubleshooting steps so that retrieval does not show only an incomplete procedure.
